comparison: Both evaluate claims about Piezo1's role in T cell migration (C6, C27, C28, C33-C37). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with multiple independent approaches and appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, acknowledging Piezo1 is 'implicated' but noting 'relatively moderate' effects and questioning whether it 'critically' senses mechanical cues due to lack of direct experimental evidence under varied mechanical conditions.

Both evaluate Piezo1 localization to the leading edge (C38, C39, C40). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED through multiple imaging approaches with statistical significance. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'They show that Piezo1 is redistributed to the leading edge' and noting the study provides 'useful insights into the subcellular localization.' Strong agreement on this finding.

Both evaluate membrane tension measurements and Piezo1 recruitment (C43-C47). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting quantitative IRM evidence and temporal correlation analysis. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, raising technical concerns about temporal inconsistencies where 'after ten minutes the median tension...reduce down to the pretreatment time point,' contradicting authors' claims about sustained high tension.

Both evaluate focal adhesion formation relative to Piezo1 (C57-C62). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting that pFAK and paxillin polarity remain unaffected by Piezo1 knockdown, indicating focal adhesions are upstream. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal ordering based on inhibitor experiments, though noting effects are 'relatively moderate.' Agreement on the mechanistic sequence.

Both evaluate FAK's role in Piezo1 redistribution (C64, C65, C7, C8, C30). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED through FAK inhibitor experiments showing complete abrogation of Piezo1 polarity. Peer reviewers also rate the temporal ordering SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'Piezo1 activation to be downstream of focal adhesion formation' based on the inhibitor data. Strong agreement on this mechanistic link.

Both evaluate Piezo1's role in LFA1/integrin recruitment (C66-C68, C10, C14, C32, C89). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with colocalization data and loss of LFA1 polarity in Piezo1-deficient cells. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting only 'moderate reduction of LFA-1 polarity' and questioning whether Piezo1 is 'critically' important for integrin recruitment despite observed correlation.

Both evaluate pAkt polarity and integrin signaling (C71-C73). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting selective loss of pAkt polarity while total Akt polarity is maintained, consistent with disrupted integrin signaling. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns about these findings. Agreement on this signaling cascade component.

Both evaluate Ca2+ colocalization with Piezo1 (C76, C11). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED through TIRF imaging with rigorous statistical analysis comparing to simulated random distributions. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED without challenging the calcium colocalization data, consistent with Piezo1's known function as a calcium-permeable channel.

Both evaluate calpain's role in the signaling cascade (C77, C78, C12). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED through calpain inhibitor experiments showing requirement for LFA1 recruitment but not focal adhesion formation. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED, accepting that 'Piezo1 activation to be downstream of focal adhesion formation and upstream of calpain-mediated LFA-1...recruitment.' Agreement on this mechanistic ordering.

Both evaluate F-actin polarity and its relationship to Piezo1 (C81-C86). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED through imaging data showing spatial separation and loss of F-actin polarity upon Piezo1 knockdown. Peer reviewers also rate it SUPPORTED without raising specific concerns, accepting this as consistent with the proposed migration signaling cascade.

Both evaluate the integrative mechanistic model (C13, C29, C69, C70, C87, C88). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED, noting the complete temporal sequence is validated with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, stating 'Whether Piezo1 is critically sensing mechano-physical cues...is however not well supported by direct experimental evidence,' criticizing modest effects and lack of experiments with varying mechanical conditions.

Both address membrane tension and Piezo1 recruitment mechanism (C9, C31, C63, C93 for OpenEval; C43-C47, C9 for peer). OpenEval finds the tension-based recruitment mechanism SUPPORTED through IRM data and correlation analysis. Peer reviewers raise UNCERTAIN concerns about temporal inconsistencies in tension measurements. Partial overlap with different emphases.

OpenEval evaluates directional dependencies between F-actin and LFA1 (C79, C80) as UNCERTAIN, noting the claim is speculative and would require direct F-actin manipulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific directional dependency claims.
